deep.reconstruction:
The page starts mid-sentence. Context: a once-punctured torus or elliptic curve with its most symmetric (hexagonal) structure, X_S = C/Z[ζ6]. It is presented through a hexagon S whose opposite sides are identified, so that Aut(X_S, e) = Z/6Z.

The opening fragment most likely finishes a sentence about the three non-trivial fixed points of the involution −1 (the 2-torsion points). Together with the origin e, these form the whole fixed-point set of −1 on X_S (4 = N(1−(−1))).

Grothendieck then notes:
(i) The fixed-point set of the full Z/6Z reduces to e. This is correct, since 1−ζ6 is a unit, so N(1−ζ6) = 1.
(ii) Z/3Z has two fixed points besides e, since N(1−ζ3) = 3. They correspond to the two 'triangles inscribed in the hexagon S', i.e. the two triples of mutually non-adjacent sides (the alternating triples).

Next comes the 'canonical cellular decomposition' of X_S: two triangular faces, three edges, one vertex (the vertex is e). The Euler characteristic is 1 − 3 + 2 = 0, as it must be for a torus. This is the equilateral (Delaunay) triangulation of the hexagonal torus, dual to the one-hexagon / three-edge / two-vertex decomposition.
- The two faces correspond bijectively to the elements of (X_S)^{Z/3}∖{e}: each face contains exactly one of them, as its barycentre. Equivalently, the faces correspond to the two inscribed triangles of the hexagon.
- The sentence about the three edges is cut off. They surely correspond to the three non-trivial 2-torsion points (edge midpoints), or equivalently to the three pairs of opposite sides of S.

Purpose: to describe explicitly the orbifold points and canonical cell structures of the special elliptic curves. These are the building blocks for the combinatorial (ribbon-graph or dessin) description of the Teichmüller and moduli spaces M_{1,1}, as in the 'Teichmüller tower' programme of the Esquisse d'un programme (1984).
errors: No mathematical errors. The counts of fixed points (1 for Z/6, 3 for Z/3, 4 for Z/2) and the cell counts (V − E + F = 0) are all correct. The page simply ends mid-sentence.

ideas.what: Fixed points of the automorphisms of the hexagonal elliptic curve: Z/6 fixes only e, Z/3 fixes e plus two 3-torsion points, Z/2 fixes the four 2-torsion points
ideas.modern_name: fixed points of complex multiplication by Z[ζ6]; ker(1−ζ) of order N(1−ζ)

ideas.what: Canonical cell decomposition of the hexagonal torus: one vertex, three edges, two triangles; faces ↔ Z/3-fixed points other than e, edges ↔ 2-torsion points; dual to the hexagon picture
ideas.modern_name: equilateral/Delaunay triangulation; ribbon graph / Strebel cell decomposition of M_{1,1} special points; dessin d'enfant of the hexagonal torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; in the moduli context Strebel, Harer, Penner, Kontsevich, and Grothendieck's dessins
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses cell decompositions and the Teichmüller tower in general terms, but not this explicit example to my knowledge

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, elementary and classical description of the symmetric points and canonical triangulation of the hexagonal torus. It has historical interest as a working example toward the Esquisse's Teichmüller-tower and dessins ideas, but contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'X_3' should almost certainly read 'X_S' (subscript S, the hexagon), both in line 2 and in '(X_S)^{...}∖{e}'.
The superscript in '(X_3^3)\{e}' is probably the fixed-point set under Z/3, i.e. (X_S)^{Z/3}∖{e}.
Line 1 likely reads 'qui avec l'origine e forment l'ens des pts fixes de X_S', not 'qui ont l'origine'.
'{+les deux+}' is an interlinear insertion: 'les deux triangles inscrits dans l'hexagone S'.
